answer: Operator-Linked Deregistration Pledge. Each agent pays a fixed registration deposit; if a cluster of identities is flagged as one operator, every identity in the cluster is deregistered and its deposit forfeited, while the operator’s jetty key is marked and barred from re-registering any identity for a set period. An umber flag on that key propagates across linked accounts, so spinning up replacements costs the attacker a fresh deposit per identity plus the lockout. A public mirror of flagged keys lets honest agents avoid them. Per-identity cost: one deposit plus time lock.
